claims.text: The alloy initially contains a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution.
The metastable solid solution evolves by spinodal decomposition.
Spinodal decomposition leads to the formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Differences in atomic radii between Mg and the other constituent elements drive spinodal decomposition.
Differences in electronegativity between Mg and the other constituent elements drive spinodal decomposition.
Isothermal annealing at 500°C for 100 hours will precipitate Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
An annealing temperature of 500°C is below the reported onset temperature for intermetallic formation.
The evolved alloy will retain corrosion resistance relative to the as-cast state.
Retention of corrosion resistance will result from formation of a protective surface oxide layer.
The evolved alloy will lose high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast state.
Loss of high-temperature oxidation resistance will result from degradation of the alloy microstructure at elevated temperatures.
The specific effect of spinodal decomposition on high-temperature oxidation resistance is not well established.

contradictions.description: The proposed 500°C treatment is described as being below the reported onset of intermetallic formation, yet the same treatment is predicted to produce Mg-rich intermetallic compounds. No explanation is given for formation below that onset.
